summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B expands the direct and second-order public-company map for the supplier-risk, resilience, testing, certification, and procurement-intelligence node. The cleanest direct public exposure is testing/inspection/certification and utility/grid analytics rather than generic enterprise software. The two-lane list uses UL Solutions as the reference TIC leader, then focuses the discovery lane on TIC Solutions, Willdan, and Itron as smaller or more niche public companies tied to utility resilience, grid planning, asset integrity, inspections, certification, and analytics. Claims are deliberately conservative because this node is still a speculative_shadow lane and requires later verification of energy-specific revenue concentration, recurring software mix, utility customer penetration, and whether supplier-risk complexity translates into measurable orders or margins. This Layer 1B pass expands a speculative second-order node around energy supplier-risk visibility, utility asset resilience, testing/certification, and procurement/operations analytics. The investable US-listed map is fragmented: pure-play energy supplier-risk software appears scarce, so the strongest public candidates cluster in adjacent lanes: supplier-risk data platforms, electrical testing/certification, grid-edge utility analytics, and utility infrastructure inspection/geospatial services. The underfollowed lane is most plausible in ITRI and NVEE, while SPGI and ULS serve as higher-attention reference anchors for supplier-risk intelligence and certification bottlenecks.
